Drug trafficking appears only in a fronted participial phrase, while the sentence's point is the toll of illicit arms (3.2).

The campaign against the trafficking of small arms is organized_crime whoever receives the weapons (4.4).
Killings, arson, assaults and torture are the acts described as terrorism, with no police conduct, detention or crime in general discussed (4.9).

Stemming the illicit trafficking in small arms is organized_crime whoever receives the weapons (4.4).

Implementing the Programme of Action against the illicit small arms trade is organized_crime whoever receives the weapons (4.4).

Weapons outpacing the conventions of peace and the call for a world security system concern arms control and collective security, not peace as a value (4.10).

Security Council resolution 2634 on piracy is Council action, which is peace even for criminal violence (4.10).

The review of the Programme of Action against the illicit small arms trade and instruments to mark and trace the weapons are organized_crime whoever receives them (4.4).

The sentence treats the terrorist group's alliance with drug trafficking, called the country's most powerful transnational force, as a crime-terror nexus as such (5.1).
